_doc: DELLHOLLOW — THE CINEMATIC CAMERAS. Hand-authored companion to dellhollow.map.json:
the town played as a sequence of FIXED pre-rendered shots (the FF7/8/9 grammar).
This file is DATA and it is the ONLY place a shot is defined. Adding, removing,
re-aiming or re-splitting a camera is an edit HERE plus two re-runs:
node tools/cine_solve.mjs        -> dellhollow.cameras.solved.json (framing solved
against townwalk's walk geometry; a build artifact)
node tools/scenegraph_derive.mjs -> public/world/scenegraph.json (the silent cut edges)
Blender -b tools/blends/dellhollow-master.blend -P tools/cine_bake.py -- <ids...>
-> public/assets/scenes/del-cine/ (the art + depth)
No camera id, region, radius or shot lives in any .js/.py/.html file.
OWNERSHIP IS THE COVERAGE CONTRACT. Every camera OWNS a set of the town map's
landmarks and a set of its walk edges, and the union must be the WHOLE town — that
is what makes 'every walkable area is reachable through static cameras alone' a
checkable claim instead of a hope. Ownership is by MAP RECORD, not by polygon,
because the town's walk meshes are named after the records that made them
(walk_pad_<landmark>, walk_lm_<landmark>, walk_e_<from>__<to>_*), so every one of
townwalk's 315 walk_ meshes has exactly one owner by construction and tools/
cine_test.mjs can prove it. The xz polygon each camera owns is DERIVED from that
ownership (the hull of its walk meshes) — see the solved file.
landmarks: [ '<landmark id>', ... ]
edges:     [ '<from>__<to>', ... ]  the map edge, whole
[ '<from>__<to>@0..0.45', ... ]  a FRACTION of it, measured along the
edge's own polyline from `from` to `to`. Ranges on one edge must tile
[0,1]. This is how a long boardwalk or a deep flight is split between
two shots, and the cut then lands MID-EDGE — which is exactly the FF
move of the camera changing as you walk on.
FRAMING IS INTENT, NOT A TRANSFORM. A shot states where it looks FROM and how much
air it wants; tools/cine_solve.mjs solves the STANDOFF so the owned region is
actually in frame, and reports the character's on-screen height so legibility is a
measured number and not a hope. Author `pos`/`aim` explicitly only to reproduce a
shot a human already accepted (the Boatyard v10 hero camera).
yaw    degrees, the direction FROM the aim point TO the camera in the map's xy
plane. 0 = +x (downstream / north), 90 = +y (out over the river, away from
the cliff), 180 = -x (upstream), 270 = -y (into the cliff face).
pitch  degrees the camera sits above the aim point. Dellhollow is a canyon wall:
y=0 is the cliff top, y~30 is the river, and height falls with y, so most
shots stand out over the gorge (yaw near 90) and look back into the wall.
fov    VERTICAL degrees. 35 is the projection canon (MIGRATION.md, user-ratified).
margin fraction of the frame kept clear around the owned region (0.10 = a 10%
border). Bigger = more air, smaller character.
aimLift metres the aim point rises above the walk surface (eye/head height).
maxDist hard cap on the solved standoff. Hitting it means the shot cannot hold
the whole region and the region wants splitting — the solver says so.
ARRIVALS ARE DERIVED, AND MAY BE OVERRIDDEN. Where a cut puts you down is computed:
the first point along the path that is clear of the band (cutClearance). That is the
right default and it is blind to exactly one thing — what the camera can SEE. A derived
arrival can land a player behind a house, under the flight they just walked down, or
inside the shot's own hero prop, and no amount of clearance fixes it, because clearance
is a fact about the BAND and not about the sightline. So a shot may name a better
standing point, per incoming edge, in its own record:
arrivals: { '<from>__<to>:<sending camera>': [x, y, z] }   RUNTIME coords [x, up, -y]
The key carries the SENDING camera because one shot can receive two arrivals on one
edge (the Crossing is entered from both ends of the same bridge) and the edge alone
would silently pick one.
A DOOR arrival is overridable in the same layer, on the camera that OWNS the
landmark, keyed on the door instead of on an edge:
arrivals: { 'door:<landmark id>': [x, y, z] }             RUNTIME coords [x, up, -y]
It is needed because the door derivation is blinder than the cut one: scenegraph_
derive's streetDir picks which way to step off the pad by an ALPHABETICAL tie-break
between equally flat roads, and at the weapon shop that chose the one direction its
own camera cannot see. scenegraph_derive checks it (on the walk network; outside the
door's own trigger radius) and REJECTS it loudly, keeping the derived point.
AN OVERRIDE IS A PROPOSAL, NOT A FACT. cine_regions.cutGeometry checks every one and
REJECTS it loudly unless it is on the walk network, on THIS camera's own ground (else
the positional safety net corrects the camera straight back), outside the band it just
crossed, and no worse than the derived point for clearance. Of the first six ever
authored the checker caught two: one that stood on the neighbouring shot's road, and
one whose coordinate had never been converted out of map order and sat 29 m in the air.
ENTRANCES AND EXITS MUST BE IN FRAME. The map's walk edges say where a player can
arrive in a region; every one of those crossings is a cut, and tools/cine_test.mjs
projects each cut's spawn point through the camera that receives it. A player must
never materialise off-screen. That is why the cameras came after the wiring.

defaults._cutClearance_why: 2026-07-31 hotfix: 1.0 left the deep-stairs<->waterfront arrival at +0.012 past its own band on the switchback — one step re-triggered the cut backwards, a hard progression loop (user hit it live). 1.6 forces every arrival a real stride past the band it crossed.
defaults._exposure_why: The town's grade, and the ONE place it is written: cine_bake.py grades every backdrop from here (through the solved file) and tools/look_golden.py asserts the master blend agrees, so the blend and the deliverable cannot drift. 2026-07-30: -0.52 -> +0.15 with the ratified late-afternoon key (probe variant C). The old number was a dusk rig's pull-down and the single biggest reason the backdrops read brown.
_doc_cut: A camera-to-camera cut is a BAND across the walk corridor, not a circle: on an
11 m harbour deck a 1.7 m trigger sphere is a thing you walk around, and a cut
you can walk around is a camera that never changes. cutThickness is the band's
half-depth along the path; its half-width is measured from the walk surface
itself at bake time (+cutWidthPad, capped at cutWidthMax).
cutOffset: how far past a landmark's pad the seam sits. cutClearance: how far
PAST the band, measured on its own normal, the arrival must sit — arc-length
back-off (cutBackoff, now only a fallback) is not enough on a switchback, where
2.4 m along an S-bend flight is 0.7 m along the seam normal and the arrival lands
back inside the band it just came through.
defaults._doc_minDist: floor on the solved standoff. A small region fits from very close, and a camera four metres from a market stall is standing inside it — worse, this town's districts are still being built, so a shot solved against gray blockout must leave room for the geometry that replaces it.
defaults._frameExits_why: RULED ON 2026-07-31 (was a migration flag): every shot frames the seams it exits by — the solver default new towns inherit. Turned on with the full-town re-bake; lockhead/cottage re-aimed to pay for it (surgeon's frameExits diff, seam-canon §9).

cameras.name: The Valley Gate
cameras.shot: Arrival. Standing inside the town on the rim road, looking back upstream at the arch: the gatehouse toll window left, the porters' yard beyond it, the cargo winch head on the right shoulder, and the drop into the gorge past the rail. The road runs away from camera so the arch reads as a threshold you came through.
cameras._framing_note: yaw 125 stair-test FAILED BACKWARDS (14.6->6.1% stair visibility, measured post-bake) — reverted to the 68 arrival composition 2026-07-31; the gate stair is the art pass's row now, not a camera's. Pitch 28 stays (harmless).

cameras.name: The Shelf — shop street, west
cameras.shot: Down the shop street eastward, with the gate stair folded in: the S-bend flight comes down off the rim into the top of frame, the Boatmen's Rest sits front-left with its sign, the chandlery and weapon shop recede east, everyday lanterns strung overhead and gorge air past the rail on the right. You see the whole arrival into the town's living street in one shot.
cameras._framing_note: Re-aimed twice. First from yaw 158 to 140 (the map draft's own yaw) when the sweep showed 158 at 37.5% visible. Then, once this shot absorbed the gate stair, its region reached back to x17.5 and the GATE DISTRICT'S GROUND stood in the sightline — measured in the runtime through the shipped depth map at 0.38 visible, with gate_ground accounting for 7 of 10 occlusions. yaw 120 clears it at 67% (Blender probes) and comes 3 m closer, so the street reads better AND the character is bigger. The lesson: a shot has to be re-checked when its REGION changes, not only when its angle does.
cameras._arrivals_why: COMING BACK WEST OFF THE ARMOUR SHOP, THE PLAYER LANDED SOMEWHERE THIS SHOT CANNOT SEE. tools/arrival_probe.py against the shipped depth plate: the derived arrival [37.896, 19.04, -5.527] draws 91 of 91 body samples ON SCREEN and 0 survive the depth test — seam-canon §9.2 at the one frame it costs most, and §10.2's 'arrives invisible' sub-signal. The occluder is the weapon shop's OWN building: ray-cast from the solved pos, 58 of 63 rays at this stretch of street stop on shelf_weapon_shop. [39.0, 19.04, -4.3] is the far corner of walk_pad_weapon-shop, on this camera's own ground, chest 100% / body 100% visible. It clears the band by 0.86 m against the derived point's 1.60 — under the 1.6 m target and well over the 0.5 m floor, so cutGeometry accepts it with the documented warning: clearance traded for an arrival the camera can actually SEE. NOT FIXED HERE: the weapon shop's DOOR arrival is 0% visible too, and a grid scan of every walkable sample within 5 m found NO point that is >= 1.85 m from the door, clear of this band and visible — see the DAYLOG on this shot's yaw 120 -> 40.
cameras._owns_note: valley-gate__inn (the gate stair) was briefly its own transit shot. It is a 7 m flight with BOTH endpoints owned by other cameras, which is the same structural fault the loop stairs had: it needs two seams inside seven metres, and once the placer was also required to keep seams off the rim road it slid them to 0.5 m apart. A 7 m flight does not get its own screen in any FF field map either — it belongs to the street it delivers you to.

cameras.name: The Shelf — shop street, east
cameras.shot: Looking back westward up the street: the armour shop cantilevered out over the void on the left, the shop row receding toward the inn, the shelf homes closing the frame at the far end where the street turns down into the market.

cameras.name: The Loop Stairs
cameras.shot: The double descent: the shelf homes' little yard at the top of frame and TWO flights leaving it, turning down five metres onto the quay — one to the harbour deck, one straight into the market. Shot from out over the gorge so the whole tier stack reads at once: shelf lanterns above, stall canvas below, gorge air between them.
cameras._framing_note: This shot owns the JUNCTION (shelf-homes) as well as both flights, and that is the whole point. The flights are only 6.5 m and 8.3 m long on the ground while dropping 5 m; when a transit shot owned a flight but not its head, BOTH of the flight's endpoints belonged to other cameras, so it needed two seams inside seven metres and the placer slid them to 0.4 m apart — two camera cuts in half a metre, which no FF field screen has ever done. Owning the junction gives each flight exactly ONE seam, at its foot, on flat ground.
cameras._arrivals_why: shelf_home_a: she arrived behind a house, 403/403 samples occluded. 2.56 m along the yard; 100% -> 0.0%.

cameras.name: The Harbour Deck
cameras.shot: The heart of the town, from over the gorge at deck level: the cookhouse glow on the left, the notice board mid-deck, the open crowd space of the harbour deck, and the deep stairs' shadowed corner far left. The Shelf's lights stack up the wall behind.

cameras.name: The Lockhead
cameras.shot: The overlook, from high out over the basin: the harbourmistress's post at the deck's end, the long plank approach running away toward it, the maintenance ladder plunging off the edge, and Lock Five with the dam small and thunderous far below.

cameras.name: Keepers' Spur
cameras.shot: Intimate, from out over the basin: the keepers' cottage set against the cliff with its balcony over the drop, warm windows, and the path from the Lockhead climbing into frame from the left.

cameras.name: The Crossing
cameras.shot: The postcard: side-on to the span, the plank bridge sagging across frame with the basin far below, bunting snapping in the gorge wind, cottage lights waiting at the far end. TRANSIT VIGNETTE (map parcel p-crossing) — no landmarks by design.
cameras._thresholdPair_why: A place you ENTER and LEAVE: it owns the middle of one map edge whose two ends belong to other shots, so its passage costs two cuts BY DESIGN. Both sit at the span's own thresholds (abutment, stair head/foot), never mid-plank. seam_test.mjs allows the second cut only for a camera that declares this.
cameras._arrivals_why: cx_approach, the bridge approach ramp. 6.50 m out onto the span; 45.2% -> 0.7%. NOTE: this is the town's LONGEST cut teleport at 6.50 m, past the 4.15 m the rest of the town tops out at — kept because the alternative is a 45% occluded arrival, and flagged for ruling.

cameras.name: The Weave
cameras.shot: From the cliff shoulder out over the stilt clusters — the pilot cluster's plank yard, the huts stacked on their legs, drying decks strung with nets, the Westweave tucked in under the quay's shadow, and the gorge wall receding behind. The pilot slice's proven drama angle.

cameras.name: The Deep Stairs
cameras.shot: The town's hidden vertical: thirteen metres of switchback flight pinned to the cliff, shot side-on so the whole zig-zag reads at once — the head's shadowed mouth at the top, the boardwalk light at the foot. No landmarks by design.
cameras._thresholdPair_why: A place you ENTER and LEAVE: it owns the middle of one map edge whose two ends belong to other shots, so its passage costs two cuts BY DESIGN. Both sit at the span's own thresholds (abutment, stair head/foot), never mid-plank. seam_test.mjs allows the second cut only for a camera that declares this.

cameras.name: The Boatyard
cameras.shot: The ACCEPTED Boatyard v10 hero shot, reproduced exactly: low along the slipway looking upstream, hauled hulls looming over the ways, the boatwright's shed and pitch kettle to the right, Lock Four closing the view. Explicit pos/aim — a human accepted this frame, so the solver does not get to move it.
cameras._owns_note: winch-foot__slipway is split at 0.52 rather than at the boatyard's own edge because the v10 hero frame is composed LOW along the slipway and its bottom edge cuts the near boardwalk: with the seam closer to camera, a player arriving from the Waterfront came in with their feet below frame (screen y -1.13). The shot is accepted and does not move, so the OWNERSHIP moved instead.
cameras._framing_note: 2026-07-31: water-side yaw 90 restored — the as-built cliff refuted every cliff-side position (measured: continuous ridge h 9.3..15.3 at y~18 across x 4..32, camera was 4.5m behind it, 0.0%% visible). Water 38.9%%, charPx far 58->67. v10 hero frame remains in git as fallback.
cameras._arrivals_why: hero_hull_clinker — the hauled hull on the ways, this shot's own hero prop — stood 4.75 m in front of her feet. 1.30 m along the boardwalk clears it; 100% -> 0.0% occluded (vista custodian, ghost test).

cameras.name: The Waterfront — winch foot
cameras.shot: The boardwalk's upstream run under the cliff: the cargo winch platform and its dangling hook, the discreet mouth of the deep stairs vanishing up into shadow behind it, fish racks starting downstream. Water on the right the whole way.
cameras._framing_note: Re-aimed from yaw 146 / pitch 14 (36% visible — the cliff the boardwalk is cut into was in the way) to a position just out over the water downstream, looking back UP the boardwalk so it recedes: 80% visible at 17.7 m. The sweep's top answer (yaw 60) sat 43 m out, past the river and inside the far canyon wall's airspace; this one is the same score from somewhere a camera can actually be.

cameras.name: The Fish Dock
cameras.shot: Downstream along the same boardwalk: the fish dock's plank apron and drying racks filling frame, the Weave's stilt legs and its ladder coming down on the left, the shack and the moorage opening away east.
cameras._framing_note: The waterfront was ONE camera and its far figure measured 34 px of 768 over a 41.5 m boardwalk. No fov or margin fixes that — the far figure's size is set by how many character-heights of region the shot must hold, so the only lever is splitting. Two shots, seam mid-boardwalk (fish-dock__winch-foot@0.45), which is the FF move anyway: the camera changes as you walk on.

cameras.name: The Keepers' Steps
cameras.shot: The last descent, read broadside: the cottage stair zig-zagging eight metres down the spur face with the cottage lit above it, the basin opening to the right, Lock Five past the moorage. No landmarks by design.
cameras._thresholdPair_why: A place you ENTER and LEAVE: it owns the middle of one map edge whose two ends belong to other shots, so its passage costs two cuts BY DESIGN. Both sit at the span's own thresholds (abutment, stair head/foot), never mid-plank. seam_test.mjs allows the second cut only for a camera that declares this.
cameras._framing_note: THIRD framing, and the first chosen against a MEASURED arrival. yaw 128 (out over the water) and yaw 330 (downstream, cliff-side) both stood on the CLIFF side of a switchback whose arrival sits on its river face, so the player materialised UNDER the flight she had just walked down, behind its own treads and handrails: nav-eval 0/5 with wentBack 5/5, shot_probe, and a 351-cell ghost sweep whose best legal standing cell was still 64.8% occluded. Three instruments agreeing makes it the CAMERA row per seam-canon 9.3 - every occluder named is the walk graph itself, which is nobody to trim. yaw 45 is not a taste pick: the flight runs (92.6,22)->(86.9,28), so its own axis is 45 degrees, and 45 is the BROADSIDE of it. Every blocker measured off the shipped depth plate falls on the far side. Probe-rendered before committing (docs/qa/districts/cs45_cottage-steps.png) after yaw 0 was rendered and REJECTED - it cleared the blockers too but read as a town vista with the flight edge-on and lost in it. Water 66.8% -> 8.4%, traded knowingly on the brief order (trade water before arrival visibility). Wall clearance 0.8m -> 7.8m: the old frame was nearly inside the as-built cliff.

cameras.name: Lock Five
cameras.shot: The water-level centrepiece, low in the gorge looking downstream: the black dam and its three wheels ahead, the lock gates, the tar-dark boat at its moorage, the tenant's shack on the near bank, and the cottage lantern-lit on the wall above — the 'house over the locks' sightline.
cameras._arrivals_why: wv_planking: she arrived UNDER the drying decks, 10.77 m of them nearer than her own feet. 3.75 m out to the moorage; 91% visible. The 6.96 m alternative reached 0.7% occlusion and was REFUSED by the coordinator — a 7 m jump would be the town's new worst teleport outlier by 68%.

cameras.name: North Landing
cameras.shot: The last pier and the goodbye shot: from out on the water looking back upstream, the dam's black mass and wheels behind, the whole town stacked up the cliff above it. The night-departure stage.

_PROPOSAL: NOT SHIPPED DATA. This is the camera file proposed by docs/plans/quay-junction-surgery.md,
kept beside it so the coordinator can diff it against public/townmap/dellhollow.cameras.json
and so anyone can re-verify the claim in one command:
It carries the _doc/_framing_note prose of the file it was derived from; those notes on
quay-east (deleted) and boatyard (pin lifted) are stale BY DESIGN and are rewritten when
the coordinator applies the change to the real file.
